blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Government of India Act, 1935 granted provincial autonomy and laid the constitutional framework for India.
Congress ministries served from 1937 to 1939 but resigned in protest against India's forced involvement in World War II.
The Quit India Movement (1942) was the final and largest mass upsurge demanding immediate end to British rule.
Subhas Chandra Bose and the Indian National Army (INA) posed a direct military threat to the British Empire.
The Mountbatten Plan (1947) finalized partition, leading to the legal end of British rule via the Indian Independence Act.

items: Government of India Act 1935 abolished provincial dyarchy and introduced provincial autonomy.
Congress ministries resigned in October 1939 over unilateral involvement in WWII; Muslim League celebrated 'Day of Deliverance' on Dec 22, 1939.
Quit India Resolution was passed on August 8, 1942 at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, with Gandhi's call to 'Do or Die'.
Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) rejected the partition demand and proposed a federal structure with provincial grouping.
